sentence: This project studies how metabolic enzymes help environmental chemicals cause changes in the epigenome that persist through development.
This project tries to find out how a receptor system affects morphine pain relief and separates helpful effects of opioids from harmful ones.
This project tries to find out how sensory neurons activate a receptor on colonic mast cells, causing pain and barrier problems in irritable bowel syndrome.
This project tries to find out how alcohol changes inhibitory neurons linking the insular cortex to the striatum and how that drives binge drinking.
This project improves the safety practices, facilities and research abilities of a laboratory that studies pathogens and tests diagnostics, therapeutics and vaccines.
This project uses an instrument combining optical tweezers, fluorescence imaging and microfluidics to study how biomolecules work in normal and disease states.
This project tries to make tumors easier for the immune system to detect by using small molecules that trigger an inflammatory form of cell death.
This project studies whether infections with certain viruses or specific autoantibodies are linked to faster progression of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
This project builds nanoparticles and biomaterials that deliver nucleic acids into dendritic cells, macrophages and T cells to change how they react to antigens.
This project develops an MRI method that images oxygen and air in the lungs during free-breathing and studies several chronic lung diseases.
This project studies how genetic recombination shapes the evolution of bacteria and how their genes and alleles change in populations.
This project uses a platform that classifies hard-to-interpret DNA variants linked to Alzheimer's disease so that risk can be assessed earlier.
This project tests whether a short course of immunotherapy before surgery can change liver cancers so that patients are cured more often.
This project tests in a randomized trial whether varenicline treats cannabis use disorder, and uses machine-learning to find who responds.
This project studies how cell competition and fitness affect chronic liver disease, using growth-advantaged liver cells.
This project uses mobile technology to study how daily activities and social situations change how much people value cannabis and how much they use.
This project develops an intervention to help people in safety-net health settings get timely follow-up care after an abnormal cervical cancer screening test.
This project studies pathogen biology and disease pathogenesis, plus the ecology of disease and the role of vectors in pathogen transmission.
